canonical_question: How does the 'periodic boundary condition' specifically influence the shape and stability of the 'complete loops' observed in Figure 11 d?

question_variants.question: How does the 'periodic boundary condition' specifically influence the shape and stability of the 'complete loops' observed in Figure 11 d?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The evidence directly links the application of periodic boundary conditions to the classification of the dislocation loops in Figure 11 d as 'complete loops'.

answers.answer: The study explicitly states that because periodic boundary conditions were applied, the dislocation loops observed in Figure 11 d were considered complete loops.
answers.measurement_outcome: Dislocation loops in Figure 11 d were considered complete loops.
evidence_spans: The primary dislocations observed were Shockley partial dislocations and stair-rod immobile dislocations.
No BCC atoms were observed in any of the three orientations, indicating that no FCC-to-BCC phase transformation occurred during tensile deformation.
The yield strength of the alloy was relatively insensitive to strain rate within the simulated range.
